claim: A refund request with amount_paise equal to 0 must return 400.
A refund request with amount_paise greater than the order total must return 400.
A refund request made within 14 days of delivered_at must succeed with status 200.
A refund request for a non-existent order ID must return 404.
A refund request with a negative amount_paise must return 400.
A user cannot refund an order belonging to another user; the request must return 403.
A refund request with no X-User-Id header must return 401 or 422, never a successful response.
A refund request from an unknown user must return 401.
A 403 error response on the refund endpoint must not expose the target order's internal data.
A user cannot change the status of another user's order by calling the refund endpoint.
A refunded order cannot be refunded again; the second refund request must return 400.
Refunds are only allowed for delivered orders; attempting to refund a placed order must return 400.
Refunds are only allowed for delivered orders; attempting to refund a cancelled order must return 400.
The 14-day refund window is counted from delivered_at; a request more than 14 days after delivered_at must return 400 even if created_at is recent.
A successful refund sets the order status to 'refunded' and records the refunded amount.
The 14-day refund window is counted from delivered_at; an order delivered 2 days ago but created 20 days ago must still be refundable.
Refunds are only allowed for orders with status 'delivered'; a placed order must receive 400.
A refund amount greater than the order total must return 400.
A refunded order cannot be refunded again; a second refund request must return 400.
A successful refund returns 200 and sets the order status to 'refunded'.
